name: Longquan celadon
summary: Green-glazed stoneware and porcelain from the kilns of Longquan. Potters built up thick layers of glaze that fire to a soft jade-green, with a plain form that gives the glaze all the beauty.

philosophy.core_thesis: A vessel reaches beauty when the glaze alone makes it: a thick, quiet green like jade that hides all other ornament.
design_principles: Apply the glaze in 3 to 8 thin layers, with a firing or a drying between layers.
Reach a glaze 1 to 2 mm thick that is opaque, soft and rich in tone.
Fire in strong reduction at 1200 to 1280 °C, so that the iron turns the glaze green.
Use a plain, strong shape with a clean profile; let the glaze be the decoration.
Add only low relief, incised lines or applied moulded figures, under the glaze.
Wipe the glaze off the foot ring, or leave a small part bare so that it turns orange in the fire.
Choose pale blue-green (fenqing) or deeper plum-green (meizi qing) glaze, never a mixed palette.
anti_patterns: Bright painted decoration on the glaze
A thin transparent glaze that shows the body
A brown, olive or yellow cast from weak reduction
Elaborate shapes with sharp edges that break the glaze flow
Gilding or applied enamels on the green

form.shape: Plum vases, bottle vases, dishes, large chargers, incense burners and kinuta (mallet-shaped) vases.
form.profile: A full, smooth belly and a short neck; the silhouette stays calm and unbroken.
form.foot_and_rim: A thin foot ring that is bare of glaze and fires red-brown; a thin lip and a clean edge.
form.proportion: Vase height 20 to 40 cm and a wall 3 to 8 mm thick; a charger diameter up to 60 cm.
rules: Keep the profile simple, so that the glaze flows evenly over it.
Use a thick foot ring on a large piece to carry the weight.
Place relief decoration low, under the thick glaze, so the glaze softens it.
Leave the foot ring unglazed and bright orange.

bodies.rule: Use a pale, dense body of porcelain stone and clay that fires grey-white. It must carry a thick glaze without slumping.

forming.joins: Parts of a large vase are thrown and joined at the shoulder; handles and applied figures are luted with slip.
forming.details: An orange-red unglazed ring at the foot, a thin brown line at the rim where the glaze thins, and a smooth, thick glaze edge at the base.

glaze.pattern: A plain glaze field; relief lotus petals, double fish or a dragon, only as a low shape under the glaze.
glaze.gloss: Soft satin to gloss, about 40 to 65 GU, with the depth of jade.
glaze.wear: Light crackle may appear in a deliberate net; the green stays stable and the foot ring darkens.

palette.strategy: One family of greens, from a pale sea-blue green to a deep plum green, and an orange-red foot.

firing.kiln: A long dragon kiln that climbs a hillside, fired with wood; one kiln holds thousands of pieces.
firing.scale: Hundreds of kilns in Longquan county made ware for the court and for export by sea.
firing.signs: A thick glaze edge near the foot, bubbles in the glaze, spur marks, and an orange unglazed ring.

pieces.form: Plum vase (meiping) with a small mouth and a broad shoulder, in pale green glaze
Large dish with a double-fish relief in the well and a thick plum-green glaze
Mallet-shaped vase with two fish handles in a soft pale glaze
Deep bowl with moulded lotus petals on the outside and a crackled glaze

positive: low relief lotus petals under glaze
pale blue-green with soft light reflection

lineage.root: It grows from the older Yue celadon of Zhejiang, which is not a style in this data.

emotion.target_response: A cool, deep calm: the viewer looks into a thick green glaze and feels stillness and restraint.

use_cases: a quiet vase for a calm interior
a museum label on Song and Yuan celadon
a prompt for a pale green glaze study
avoid_when: the brief needs painted pattern or bright colour
the brief needs an earthenware body

modifiers.how: Keep the green glaze, thin it to a transparent grey-green, and add inlaid white and black slip patterns.
Change to a white porcelain, remove the green and paint cobalt under a clear glaze.
